column1: admonish§The coach admonished her for arguing with the referee.§教练因她与裁判争辩而**告诫**了她。§
adulate§Reporters adulated the young champion until the first defeat.§记者们把这位年轻冠军**捧上天**，直到他第一次失利。§
agonize§He agonized over the wording for the better part of a week.§他为措辞**苦苦思索**了大半个星期。§
apostle§She became an apostle of plain language in government forms.§她成了政府表格用平实语言的**倡导者**。§
assume§Do not assume the reader knows what the abbreviation stands for.§不要**假设**读者知道这个缩写代表什么。§
blithe§His blithe assurance that it would sort itself out annoyed everyone.§他**漫不经心**地保证事情会自行解决，惹恼了所有人。§
bluff§He was bluffing, and the other side called it.§他是在**虚张声势**，对方识破了。§
breed§The farm breeds sheep suited to wet upland pasture.§这个农场**培育**适应潮湿高地牧场的绵羊。§
chagrin§To his chagrin, the error was on the very first slide.§让他**懊恼**的是，错误就出在第一张幻灯片上。§
cinematography§The cinematography does more storytelling than the script.§这部片子的**摄影**比剧本更会讲故事。§
clemency§The governor granted clemency in the last week of his term.§州长在任期最后一周给予了**宽赦**。§
commensurate§The fee should be commensurate with the work involved.§收费应当与所付出的工作**相称**。§
conciliate§A short apology conciliated a neighbor of thirty years.§一句简短的道歉**安抚**了相处三十年的邻居。§
contaminate§One cracked seal contaminated the entire batch.§一处开裂的密封圈**污染**了整批产品。§
contempt§His contempt for the process showed in every answer.§他对这套程序的**轻蔑**体现在每一个回答里。§
courageous§It was courageous to publish the figures under her own name.§用自己的名字公布这些数字是**需要勇气**的。§
defect§A defect in the casting was found only after installation.§铸件的一处**缺陷**直到安装后才被发现。§
detriment§He worked through the summer to the detriment of his health.§他整个夏天都在工作，**损害**了自己的健康。§
dissemble§She dissembled well enough that nobody guessed she was leaving.§她**掩饰**得很好，没人猜到她要走。§
draw§The exhibition drew a larger crowd than the museum could hold.§这个展览**吸引**的人数超出了博物馆的容量。§
elucidate§One diagram elucidated what three pages of text had not.§一张图**阐明**了三页文字都没说清的东西。§
emancipate§The reform emancipated tenants from a rule two centuries old.§这项改革把租户从一条两百年的旧规中**解放**出来。§
encapsulated§The final paragraph encapsulated a decade of research.§最后一段**概括**了十年的研究。§
enduring§Her enduring interest in maps began with one school atlas.§她对地图**持久的**兴趣始于一本学校地图册。§
exasperate§The third change of plan exasperated the whole crew.§第三次改计划把全体人员都**惹恼**了。§
exonerate§The recording exonerated the driver completely.§这段录音完全**免除了司机的责任**。§
extricate§It took an hour to extricate the sheep from the fence.§花了一小时才把羊从围栏里**解救**出来。§
foment§Anonymous leaflets fomented the strike.§匿名传单**煽动**了这场罢工。§
gallop§The horse galloped the length of the field and stopped dead.§那匹马沿着田野**飞奔**，然后戛然而止。§
grudgingly§He grudgingly admitted the shorter route was faster.§他**不情愿地**承认那条近路更快。§
impertinent§An impertinent question ended the interview early.§一个**无礼**的问题让面谈提早结束。§
implement§They implemented the change over a single weekend.§他们用一个周末就**实施**了这项变更。§
inadvertently§She inadvertently deleted the only copy of the file.§她**无意**中删掉了该文件的唯一副本。§
ineluctable§The conclusion is ineluctable once you read the appendix.§一读附录，这个结论就**无可回避**。§
inform§Field notes informed every decision in the final design.§田野笔记为最终设计的每个决定**提供了依据**。§
informed§An informed reader spots the omission at once.§**见多识广的**读者一眼就看出这处遗漏。§
insuperable§The language barrier proved insuperable in three days.§三天下来，语言障碍被证明是**无法克服的**。§
interject§He interjected a fact that changed the whole discussion.§他**插了一句**事实，改变了整场讨论。§
inveterate§An inveterate note-taker, she filled four books a year.§她是个**积习**难改的笔记狂，一年写满四本。§
laity§The book was written for the laity, not for specialists.§这本书是写给**外行**的，不是写给专家的。§
lash§They lashed the crates to the deck before the storm.§风暴来临前，他们把箱子**捆在**甲板上。§
make a case against§The report makes a case against building on the flood plain.§这份报告**论证了不应**在洪泛区建设。§
make a case for§She makes a case for keeping the old timetable.§她**论证了**保留旧时刻表的理由。§
obligate§The lease obligates the tenant to repair the roof.§租约使租户**有义务**修缮屋顶。§
pant§He panted at the top of the stairs and could not speak.§他在楼梯顶端**喘着气**，说不出话。§
patronize§Do not patronize an audience that knows more than you do.§不要对一群比你懂得多的听众摆出**屈尊**的姿态。§
perturbation§A small perturbation in the orbit revealed the missing planet.§轨道上的一点**扰动**揭示了那颗未被发现的行星。§
plunge§Temperatures plunged fifteen degrees overnight.§气温一夜之间**骤降**了十五度。§
postulate§He postulated a second source and later found it.§他**假设**存在第二个来源，后来果然找到了。§
predicate§The whole argument is predicated on one unverified date.§整个论证都**建立在**一个未经核实的日期上。§
preoccupation§Cost was the committee's only real preoccupation.§成本是委员会唯一**真正关心的事**。§
prone to§Clay soil is prone to cracking in a dry summer.§黏土在干燥的夏天**容易**开裂。§
provided§You may cite the letters, provided you credit the archive.§你可以引用这些信件，**前提是**注明档案出处。§
putative§The putative author of the diary was never identified.§这本日记**被认定的**作者始终未被查明。§
quench§Nothing quenched their thirst until they reached the spring.§到达泉水之前，什么都**解不了他们的渴**。§
reciprocity§The agreement rests on reciprocity rather than goodwill.§这项协议靠的是对等**互惠**，而非善意。§
refraction§Refraction makes the pole in the water look broken.§**折射**让水中的杆子看起来像断了。§
register§Her face registered nothing at all when the verdict was read.§宣读判决时，她的脸上没有**流露**任何表情。§
render§The drawing renders the harbor as it looked in 1890.§这幅画**描绘**了一八九〇年时的港口。§
repute§The firm is of good repute among people who have used it.§在用过的人当中，这家公司**口碑**不错。§
rigid§A rigid schedule left no room for the weather.§**僵硬的**日程表没给天气留出余地。§
saddle§The new rules saddled small shops with weekly paperwork.§新规让小店铺每周都**得应付**文书工作。§
secularize§The state secularized the schools in a single decade.§国家用十年时间使学校**脱离了宗教**。§
shift§Public opinion shifted sharply after the second report.§第二份报告发布后，公众舆论急剧**转变**。§
slacken§The wind slackened and the crossing became easy.§风势**减弱**，横渡变得容易了。§
staggering§The cost of the delay was staggering.§这次延误的代价**令人咋舌**。§
stymie§A missing signature stymied the whole application.§缺一个签名就**卡住**了整份申请。§
symposium§The symposium ran for three days and produced one good idea.§**研讨会**开了三天，产生了一个好想法。§
tenant§The tenant had kept every receipt for eleven years.§这位**租客**十一年来保存了每一张收据。§
testament§The bridge is a testament to careful, unglamorous work.§这座桥是细致而不起眼的工作的**见证**。§
tributary§A small tributary joins the river below the town.§一条小**支流**在镇子下游汇入这条河。§
understate§The report understates a risk it had every reason to name.§这份报告**轻描淡写**了一个它完全有理由指明的风险。§
undue§The delay caused undue hardship to the families waiting.§这次延误给等待的家庭造成了**不必要**的困难。§
virtually§The village is virtually empty between October and April.§十月到四月间，这个村子**几乎**空无一人。§
vulgar§A vulgar joke at the wrong moment cost him the room.§一个时机不对的**粗俗**玩笑让他失去了全场。§
warp§Damp had warped the door so it no longer closed.§潮气把门**弄变形**了，已经关不上。§
warrant§The evidence does not warrant a second investigation.§这些证据不足以**证明**有必要再调查一次。§
whim§The trip began as a whim and became a year's work.§这趟旅行始于**一时兴起**，后来成了一年的工作。§
wind ensemble§The school's wind ensemble played the piece from memory.§学校的**管乐团**凭记忆演奏了这首曲子。§
woeful§A woeful lack of records makes the period hard to date.§记录的**严重缺乏**使这一时期难以断代。§
